segments.source: Food relation: rabbit eats grass; fox eats rabbit; eagle eats fox. Classroom rule: if a food source sharply decreases and no alternative food is given, the consumer may also decrease. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break. Mixed-domain verification: a regional archive has 93 map sheets and receives 4 additional sheets during the exercise.

Follow dependency arrows from food to consumer. The rule supports possible directional effects, not exact population numbers. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration. For this verification, the final number of sheets equals starting sheets plus received sheets.

If rabbit sharply decreases, which later populations may be indirectly affected according to the rule? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish? Mixed-domain verification: how many sheets are available after the delivery?

1. fox depends directly on rabbit, so it may decrease. 2. eagle depends on fox, so it may also be indirectly affected. 3. grass is food for rabbit; the stated rule does not imply it decreases for the same reason. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00. Mixed-domain verification: 93+4=97.
fox may decrease directly and eagle may be affected indirectly. Cross-domain answer: 10:00. Mixed-domain answer: 97 map sheets.

N9. Renewable resources and sustainable use
Renewable does not mean unlimited. A resource can decline when use exceeds regeneration.
A forest resource starts at 140 units. Each year it regenerates 12 units and people harvest 12 units. Assume these amounts stay constant for 3 years and no other changes occur.
Annual net change = regeneration − harvest. In this simplified model, use is sustainable over the period if stock does not decline.
What is the stock after 3 years, and is the harvest sustainable under this classroom definition?
1. Annual net change=12−12=0. 2. Three-year change=0. 3. Final stock=140+(0)=140. 4. Compare final stock with starting stock.
140 units; sustainable under the stated definition.
Sustainability is a balance between renewal and extraction over time.

Problem 921. Population balance in a town: case 1
Population changes through births, deaths, immigration, and emigration.
A town begins the year with 1400 residents. During the year: births=20, deaths=14, people moving in=38, people moving out=25.
End population = start + births − deaths + in-migration − out-migration. Natural change and migration change are separate components.
Compute natural change, migration change, and the year-end population.
1. Natural change=20−14=6. 2. Migration change=38−25=13. 3. Total change=6+13=19. 4. End population=1400+19=1419.
Natural change +6; migration change +13; end population 1419.
Breaking total change into components helps explain why a population grew or shrank.
Problem 922. Population balance in a town: case 2
Population changes through births, deaths, immigration, and emigration.
A town begins the year with 1450 residents. During the year: births=23, deaths=14, people moving in=38, people moving out=29.
End population = start + births − deaths + in-migration − out-migration. Natural change and migration change are separate components.
Compute natural change, migration change, and the year-end population.
1. Natural change=23−14=9. 2. Migration change=38−29=9. 3. Total change=9+9=18. 4. End population=1450+18=1468.
Natural change +9; migration change +9; end population 1468.
Breaking total change into components helps explain why a population grew or shrank.
